entries.title: Module Documentation & Purpose
entries.why: Clear documentation upfront explains the hybrid approach: combining rule-based detection (fast, interpretable) with Isolation Forest (multivariate outliers) and LSTM (temporal patterns). This helps new developers understand the architecture before diving into code.
entries.whatItDoes: Documents the three-layer detection strategy: 1) Rule-based for known failure patterns, 2) Isolation Forest for unusual sensor combinations, 3) LSTM Autoencoder for time-series anomalies. The pipeline generates alerts with confidence scores.

entries.title: Conditional ML Library Imports
entries.why: ML libraries are heavy dependencies (TensorFlow can be 500MB+). Making them optional allows the system to run in degraded mode when libraries aren't available - critical for edge deployments or containers with size constraints.
entries.whatItDoes: Attempts to import scikit-learn and TensorFlow, setting availability flags. If imports fail, logs a warning but doesn't crash. This pattern enables graceful degradation - rule-based detection still works without ML libraries.

failureModes.recovery: System continues with rule-based and LSTM detection only
System continues with rule-based and Isolation Forest only

tests.what: Test degraded mode without ML libraries
tests.how: Mock import failures and verify pipeline still functions with rules only

entries.perfNotes: Import checks happen once at module load, no runtime overhead

entries.title: Type Definitions: Enums and Dataclasses
entries.why: Strong typing with enums and dataclasses prevents bugs from string typos and provides IDE autocomplete. The structured AnomalyResult ensures all detectors return consistent data that downstream systems can rely on.
entries.whatItDoes: Defines four key types: AnomalyType (categorizes detection method), Severity (1-4 levels), AnomalyResult (full detection output with confidence, affected sensors, recommendations), and SensorReading (normalized input format).

tests.how: Test that AnomalyResult fields behave correctly with default_factory

entries.perfNotes: Dataclasses have minimal overhead compared to dicts but provide type safety

entries.title: Rule-Based Detector: Threshold Definitions
entries.why: Rule-based detection is the first line of defense - it's fast, interpretable, and catches obvious failures. Two threshold tiers (default and critical) allow different response urgencies. Domain experts can tune thresholds without touching code.
entries.whatItDoes: Defines safe operating ranges for 8 sensor types (temperature, pressure, vibration, etc.) with units. CRITICAL_THRESHOLDS are tighter bounds that trigger immediate alerts. The class supports custom threshold overrides at initialization.

failureModes.behavior: Excessive false positives flood alert system
failureModes.recovery: Analyze historical data to calibrate appropriate thresholds

failureModes.behavior: Real anomalies missed until equipment damage occurs
failureModes.recovery: Review incident reports to identify missed patterns

tests.how: Verify values exactly at min/max thresholds are handled correctly

entries.perfNotes: O(n) where n = number of sensors, very fast

entries.title: Rule-Based Detection Logic
entries.why: The check method iterates through all sensor values, matching each to its threshold rule. The fuzzy matching (_find_threshold_key) handles sensor naming variations like 'temp_motor_1' matching 'temperature' rules.
entries.whatItDoes: For each sensor value: 1) Find matching threshold rule by name substring, 2) Check if value exceeds min/max, 3) Check critical bounds for severity, 4) Build AnomalyResult with 100% confidence (rules are deterministic).

failureModes.condition: Sensor name doesn't match any threshold key
failureModes.recovery: Add custom threshold or rename sensor to match patterns

tests.what: Test all sensor types trigger correctly
tests.how: Provide readings above/below thresholds for each sensor type
Verify critical thresholds produce CRITICAL severity

entries.title: Isolation Forest Detector Setup
entries.why: Isolation Forest excels at finding multivariate outliers - combinations of values that are individually normal but collectively unusual. It's unsupervised (no labels needed) and handles high-dimensional data well.
entries.whatItDoes: Initializes sklearn's IsolationForest with configurable contamination rate (expected outlier proportion), number of trees, and random seed for reproducibility. StandardScaler normalizes features to prevent scale bias.

failureModes.recovery: Check SKLEARN_AVAILABLE flag before creating detector
Start with 0.01 (1%) and adjust based on false positive rate

tests.how: Mock SKLEARN_AVAILABLE=False, verify RuntimeError

entries.perfNotes: n_jobs=-1 uses all CPU cores for parallel tree building

entries.title: Isolation Forest Training
entries.why: Training requires sufficient normal data to learn what 'normal' looks like. The 100-sample minimum prevents underfitting. Feature names are stored to ensure prediction-time data matches training structure.
entries.whatItDoes: Converts sensor readings to numpy matrix, fits StandardScaler for normalization, then trains the IsolationForest. Stores feature_names to validate future predictions. Sets is_fitted flag when complete.

failureModes.behavior: Training skipped with warning, is_fitted stays False
failureModes.recovery: Collect more historical data before training

failureModes.behavior: Model learns anomalies as normal, reducing detection accuracy
failureModes.recovery: Pre-filter training data using rule-based detector

tests.how: Call fit() with 50 samples, verify is_fitted=False
Verify feature_names matches unique sensors from training data

entries.perfNotes: Training is O(n * trees * log(n)), can take minutes for large datasets

entries.title: Isolation Forest Detection
entries.why: Detection must handle the case where model isn't trained or features don't match. The anomaly score (-score_samples) indicates how isolated a point is - higher means more anomalous.
entries.whatItDoes: Converts reading to matrix, scales it, gets prediction (-1=outlier) and anomaly score. For outliers, maps score to severity and identifies which features (sensors) contributed most by checking standard deviations.

failureModes.behavior: Detection skipped with warning, returns None
failureModes.recovery: Retrain model or ensure consistent sensor set

tests.how: Call detect() before fit(), verify returns None
Verify score>0.7 gives HIGH, score>0.5 gives MEDIUM

entries.perfNotes: Detection is O(trees * log(n)), very fast at runtime

entries.title: LSTM Autoencoder Detector Setup
entries.why: LSTM Autoencoders learn temporal patterns - how sensor values typically change over time. They catch gradual drift, unusual oscillations, or sequences that don't match learned patterns. The autoencoder architecture learns to compress and reconstruct normal sequences.
entries.whatItDoes: Initializes with sequence_length (timesteps per sample), latent_dim (compression size), and threshold_percentile (what reconstruction error counts as anomaly). Uses a deque to maintain rolling history of readings.

failureModes.recovery: Check TF_AVAILABLE flag before creating detector

failureModes.behavior: Need many readings before detection starts
failureModes.recovery: Balance between pattern detection and responsiveness (50 is good default)

tests.how: Mock TF_AVAILABLE=False, verify RuntimeError

entries.perfNotes: History deque has O(1) append, automatically discards old readings

entries.title: LSTM Autoencoder Architecture
entries.why: The encoder-decoder architecture compresses sequences to a latent representation, then reconstructs them. Normal patterns compress well; anomalies have high reconstruction error because they don't match learned patterns.
entries.whatItDoes: Builds a symmetric autoencoder: Encoder (LSTM 64 -> LSTM latent_dim), Bottleneck (RepeatVector), Decoder (LSTM latent_dim -> LSTM 64 -> TimeDistributed Dense). Uses MSE loss to measure reconstruction quality.

failureModes.behavior: Even normal patterns have high reconstruction error
failureModes.recovery: Increase latent_dim or reduce sequence complexity

failureModes.behavior: Model memorizes instead of learning patterns, poor generalization
failureModes.recovery: Reduce latent_dim to force meaningful compression

tests.how: Build model and verify input/output shapes match

entries.perfNotes: Model size scales with latent_dim and sequence_length, keep both reasonable

entries.title: LSTM Autoencoder Training
entries.why: Training on ONLY normal data is crucial - the model learns what normal sequences look like. The threshold is set at a high percentile of training reconstruction errors, so anything worse is likely anomalous.
entries.whatItDoes: Prepares sequences from readings, builds model, trains for specified epochs with 10% validation split. After training, computes reconstruction errors on training data to set the anomaly threshold at the specified percentile.

failureModes.behavior: Model learns anomalous patterns as normal, threshold too high
failureModes.recovery: Pre-filter training data to remove known anomalies
Need at least 2x sequence_length samples, ideally much more

tests.how: Train with sequence_length*1.5 samples, verify training skipped
Verify threshold is at specified percentile of training errors

entries.perfNotes: Training can take minutes to hours depending on data size and epochs

entries.title: LSTM Temporal Anomaly Detection
entries.why: Detection maintains a rolling history and checks if the current sequence's reconstruction error exceeds the learned threshold. This catches patterns that develop over time rather than instant spikes.
entries.whatItDoes: Adds reading to history deque, prepares sequence when enough history exists, computes reconstruction error via model.predict(). If error exceeds threshold, identifies which sensors had highest reconstruction error.

failureModes.behavior: Returns None until history fills to sequence_length
failureModes.recovery: Wait for initial buffer to fill, or reduce sequence_length
Retrain model when sensor configuration changes

tests.how: Send fewer than sequence_length readings, verify returns None
Inject sequences with known error ratios, verify severity levels

entries.perfNotes: Inference is fast but runs on every reading - consider batching for high-volume streams

entries.title: Combined Pipeline Orchestration
entries.why: The combined pipeline is the master orchestrator that runs all detectors and fuses their outputs. Having configurable enables and fusion weights allows tuning the system for different deployment scenarios.
entries.whatItDoes: Initializes each detector based on enable flags and library availability. Sets fusion weights that determine how much each detector's confidence contributes to the final score. Logs which detectors are active.

failureModes.recovery: Ensure at least rule-based detection is enabled

tests.how: Disable LSTM, verify pipeline still works with rules + IF

entries.title: Multi-Detector Fusion
entries.why: Running all detectors and fusing results provides defense in depth - each detector catches different types of anomalies. The fusion logic combines their outputs into a single actionable result.
entries.whatItDoes: Runs rule-based check (returns list), Isolation Forest (returns single result or None), and LSTM (returns single result or None). Collects all anomalies and passes to _fuse_results for combination.

failureModes.recovery: Wrap each detector in try/except with logging

tests.what: Test with all detectors returning anomalies
tests.how: Inject reading that triggers all three, verify combined result
Inject normal reading, verify is_anomaly=False

entries.perfNotes: Runs all detectors sequentially - could parallelize for latency-sensitive apps

entries.title: Result Fusion Algorithm
entries.why: Fusion combines multiple detector outputs intelligently. Using weighted confidence prevents one noisy detector from dominating. The max severity ensures we don't downgrade critical alerts.
entries.whatItDoes: Aggregates affected sensors (union), concatenates descriptions, takes max severity, computes weighted average confidence. If multiple anomaly types detected, marks as COMBINED. Returns unified AnomalyResult.

failureModes.recovery: Human review for COMBINED type anomalies

tests.how: Mock results with known confidences and weights, verify calculation
Combine LOW + HIGH anomalies, verify result is HIGH

entries.perfNotes: O(n) where n = number of anomalies, typically small

entries.title: Batch Processing Function
entries.why: Batch processing is useful for historical analysis, backfilling, or systems that process readings in chunks rather than real-time. The function converts raw dicts to typed objects and returns results as dicts for JSON serialization.
entries.whatItDoes: Iterates through raw reading dictionaries, converts each to SensorReading, runs through pipeline.detect(), and collects results. Only includes anomalies in output. Returns list of dict-serialized AnomalyResults.

failureModes.recovery: Add try/except with fallback to current time

tests.how: Provide 10 readings with 2 anomalies, verify 2 results returned

entries.perfNotes: Linear time in batch size, consider chunking for very large batches

entries.title: Example Usage and Entry Point
entries.why: The main block provides a runnable example demonstrating how to use the pipeline. It shows the typical flow: create pipeline, create reading, detect anomalies. Useful for testing and as documentation.
entries.whatItDoes: Sets up logging, creates CombinedPipeline with available detectors, creates a test SensorReading with sample values, runs detection, and prints the result summary.
entries.perfNotes: Only runs when script is executed directly, not when imported
